title: Reproduce Before Repair
text: id: CORE-013 domain: debugging title: Reproduce Before Repair tags: debugging, reproduction, software memory: I lost time fixing a bug I had not reproduced. The patch solved my guess, not the failure. I rolled back, reproduced the issue, isolated the smallest trigger, and only then changed code. Debugging begins with making the problem appear on command. Repair without reproduction is theater with a diff.

title: Reproduce Beat Reading Logs
text: id: REWARD-008 domain: reward title: Reproduce Beat Reading Logs tags: reward, debugging, reproduce memory: I read logs for too long on an intermittent crash. The useful turn came when I reproduced the crash, changed one variable, and compared against the recent deploy. The reward was a failure I could make appear on command. Logs are evidence, but reproduction gives the investigation a handle.

title: The Retrieval Budget Was Spent Carefully
text: id: LIB-014 domain: librarian title: The Retrieval Budget Was Spent Carefully tags: librarian, topk, small-model memory: A small model failed when I gave it every helpful memory. It did not become wiser; it became crowded. I spent the retrieval budget like shelf space: one memory for the task type, one for the failure risk, and sometimes one for closure. The smaller set produced the cleaner answer.
